options: A force that pulls masses toward each other
A force that only pushes things apart
A magnetic effect at the edges of planets
The reason air is warm near the ground
questions.explanation: Gravity is an attractive force between masses — the bigger the masses, the stronger the pull between them.
questions.misconception: Some picture gravity as a planet's 'air pressure' or as a pushy force; it's a pull between any two masses.

questions.prompt: In a vacuum (no air), a bowling ball and a feather are dropped together. Which hits the ground first?
options: They hit at the same time
The bowling ball first
The feather first
The bowling ball, twice as fast
questions.explanation: Without air resistance, gravity accelerates all objects identically — the bowling ball's extra mass cancels its bigger pull.
questions.misconception: Real-life staggering (feather floats) comes from air resistance; remove the air and mass stops mattering.

questions.prompt: What is Earth's gravitational field strength, commonly rounded for school calculations?
options: About 9.8 m/s²
About 1 m/s²
About 98 m/s²
About 0 m/s²
questions.explanation: Earth's gravitational field strength is about 9.8 m/s², often rounded to 10 m/s² for mental math.
questions.misconception: Picking 98 m/s² treats the field as a force; the field is an acceleration (9.8 m/s²). The newton appears only when you multiply it by a mass to get weight.

questions.prompt: What keeps a satellite from flying straight off into space?
options: Gravity keeps pulling it inward toward the planet
It has no weight in orbit
A force from the rocket engine stays on
The vacuum has nothing to push against
questions.explanation: The satellite wants to go straight, but gravity continuously bends its path inward into an orbit — it keeps 'falling around' the planet.
questions.misconception: Floating in orbit is sometimes mistaken for 'no gravity'; gravity is almost full-strength there, the satellite just keeps missing the ground.

questions.prompt: Which statement connects gravity and weight correctly?
options: Weight is the gravitational force on a mass (W = mg)
Weight is the amount of matter gravity squeezes out of an object
Gravity only matters at the surface of stars
Weight is measured in kilograms only
questions.explanation: Weight is gravity's pull on a mass, quantified as W = mg. No gravity (deep space) means no weight.
questions.misconception: Weight is force (N) from gravity — it is not a mass measurement, and deep space gravity isn't zero instantly.
